data.name: Muayyid
data.gender_notes: Muayyid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who assists and helps others, particularly in religious matters. The name Muayyid carries the meaning “Helper, Supporter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muayyid usually hope their child will grow to embody helper, supporter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Serving and supporting others on the path to righteousness.
data.etymology: Muayyid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helper, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muayyid total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Muayyid in Islamic culture holds a significant meaning as it denotes a person who offers aid and assists others in their time of need. This name is often given to a child to encourage a sense of responsibility, kindness, and compassion towards others. Muayyid is a reminder that being helpful and supportive to those around us is a crucial part of building strong community bonds, and is highly valued in Islamic society.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Muayyid holds a deeper meaning as it signifies one who actively participates in the support and guidance of others on their spiritual journey. Understanding the significance of helping others in their faith and personal growth, a Muayyid is encouraged to share their knowledge and wisdom with others, acting as a mentor or guide. In doing so, they not only help others grow spiritually but also deepen their own connection to Allah, as they engage in acts of kindness and charity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Helper, Supporter" symbolizes One who assists and helps others, particularly in religious matters.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Muayyid serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of helper, supporter.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah' mentions Muayyid al-Din al-Shirazi as the founder of the Hafsid dynasty in Ifriqiya (modern-day Tunisia) in 894 A.D. under the Aghlabid rule.
historical_references.context: Muayyid al-Din was a Berber tribal chief who seized power from the Aghlabid rulers and established the Hafsid dynasty, becoming its first ruler.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's 'Kitab al-Mawāʿiẓ wa-l-Iʿtibār bi-Dhayl ʿIlā al-Taʿrīkh' records Muayyid al-Din Biyabagh as a military commander who served under the Ayyubid ruler Saladin and played a crucial role in the Battle of Hattin (1119 A.D.) against the Crusaders.
historical_references.context: Muayyid al-Din Biyabagh was a Muslim general who led a successful charge against the Crusader forces at the Battle of Hattin, turning the tide of the battle in favor of Saladin.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Muayyid remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Ibrahim Muayyid in Dubai, UAE attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Muayyid, which means "Helper, Supporter". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.
